references.text: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the veil—the same ritual as in verse 6.
Moses sprinkled the blood on the altar seven times during the consecration of the tabernacle, showing the repeated pattern of seven sprinklings.
In the cleansing of leprosy, the priest was to sprinkle seven times—the number seven symbolizes completeness in cleansing rituals.
On the Day of Atonement, the high priest was to sprinkle blood with his finger seven times on the mercy seat—the same action before the holy place.
The priest was to sprinkle blood on the altar seven times to cleanse it—parallel to the sprinkling ritual in 4:6.
The priest was to dip his finger in the blood from the red heifer and sprinkle seven times toward the front of the tent.
Description of the veil (parokhet) in the sanctuary that separated the holy place from the most holy place.
Moses was to take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with his finger—use of the finger in blood rituals.
The book of Hebrews compares the blood of goats and bulls with Christ's blood, which cleanses the conscience—the fulfillment of Old Testament blood rituals.
Moses sprinkled blood on the tabernacle and all its vessels—without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
Through Jesus' blood we have boldness to enter the sanctuary through the veil—Christ fulfills what the veil symbolized.
